slides.title: HESSLE AUDIO
slides.subtitle: Three friends from Leeds. The most influential British club label of their generation.
slides.image_concept: Leeds city night, wet cobblestone street, distant streetlight glow
slides.image_keywords: Leeds city night wet street bokeh

slides.text:
2004. Leeds University.
Ben UFO meets Kevin McAuley — later known as Pangaea.
Two students. One shared obsession.
slides.image_concept: University dorm room, laptop and stacked vinyl records, low light
slides.image_keywords: university dorm vinyl records late night

slides.text:
2006. The queue outside Plastic People, Shoreditch.
Ben UFO meets David Kennedy —
the man who will become Ramadanman. Then Pearson Sound.
They're waiting to get into FWD>>.
The label hasn't been invented yet.
slides.image_concept: Nightclub queue silhouettes in London alley, fog, night
slides.image_keywords: nightclub queue London alley night fog silhouette

slides.text:
2007. Hessle Street, Leeds.
They name the label after the street they live on.
A radio show on SubFM.
A club night called Ruffage.
Three people playing each other's tracks.
slides.image_concept: British street name sign, brick terraced houses, grey sky
slides.image_keywords: British street sign brick terraced houses

slides.text:
Ramadanman's 'Blimey' (2008).
Sparse. Percussive. Nothing like anything else.
Ricardo Villalobos plays it.
The world notices.
slides.image_concept: Dark club, speaker cone close-up, abstract bass vibration
slides.image_keywords: dark club speaker bass vibration abstract

slides.text:
Dubstep divided.
Skrillex went one way.
Hessle Audio went the other.

No wobble. No drop.
Just pressure. Space. Rhythm.
slides.image_concept: Road fork at night, one side bright and loud, one side dark and quiet
slides.image_keywords: road fork night split two paths

slides.text:
140 BPM. Then 130. Then whatever felt right.
Jungle. House. Techno. Footwork.
They didn't care about genre.
They cared about the room.

15 years.
Over 60 releases.
Still independent.
slides.image_concept: DJ mixer close-up, two hands, low club lighting
slides.image_keywords: DJ mixer hands close-up dark club

slides.text:
'Pound for pound, the most influential British club label of their generation.'
— Crack Magazine, 2022
